recipes.name: Rib-Eye Steaks with a Soy and Ginger Marinade

steps.text: Combine soy sauce, maple syrup, garlic, ginger, mustard powder, sesame oil, and hot pepper sauce in a medium mixing bowl; mix well to blend. Add beer and stir lightly to mix.

Prepare steaks by scoring any fatty outside areas on steak with a knife (this prevents the steaks from curling when grilling). Place steaks in a casserole dish and pour marinade over. Using a fork, punch holes in steaks so that the marinade penetrates into the meat. Turn steaks over and repeat punching holes.
Cover with clear wrap or foil and let marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour to overnight.

Prepare and preheat a grill to high heat. Place steaks directly on the grill and sear one side for about 15 seconds. Turn steaks over and cook for about 5 minutes, then turn over and cook for another 5 minutes for medium-rare, depending on thickness. Test for doneness by cutting into the middle of the steak.

raw_recipe.headline: Rib-Eye Steaks with a Soy and Ginger Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This ginger soy marinade makes rib-eye steaks even more tasty. Marinade ingredients include maple syrup, beer, garlic, dry mustard, and sesame oil.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is Great ! My husband and I have tried this 4 times now - He actually requested it yesterday, definately a keeper. We don't usually marinade rib eye steaks because they are so tender anyway - but this is a nice change. Excellent Flavor !! And Oh Sooo Tender ! UPDATE - we never use to marinate ribeyes but we use this all the time now - the flavor is so good and it is so tender / just cooking steaks with seasoning just isn't the same.
Thank you for sharing this recipe. Awesome !!!

I've been using this marinade for over 20 years. It's not only great for steak but for chicken as well. When I use it for chicken I substitute teriyaki sauce for the soy and add 3/4 cup crushed pineapple with juice for a great sweet Hawaiian chicken. I reuse the leftover marinade by simmering it for several minutes to get rid of any bacteria from the chicken. This will thicken the sauce which I use for basting. Do the same with the steak marinade.

6-9-17: Very good to excellent, a little sweet; maybe cut out syrup and/or add a dash of honey in lieu of syrup. Also used marinade on asparagus & potatoes but added Montreal Seasoning. Also did for one steak so reduced sauce. Didn't have beer & used real Dijon mustard & as no beer added some EVOO. Topped w butter, covered & let rest 5 min.

This recipe will be added to my "keepers" for sure. I made this using 2 thick sirlon steaks with a little extra garlic and some Sriracha. I also added about a teaspoon of prepared Dijon mustard. I made a smaller batch of the marinade that I cooked down to make a glaze, with a couple pats of butter to finish it off. My husband is not overly fond of Steak loved it. He asked me to make later in the week after my grocery store trip.
Seared for 2 mins each side and in oven @ 375 for 8 minutes. No beer and pepper, EVO instead of sesame oil. Tasted great!!!

You just turned my kitchen into the best steakhouse in town.
I'm not a beer drinker, so I substituted 1/2 cup olive oil, and I marinated the very thick sirloin for under two hours before pan-frying it to rare perfection and topping it with herb butter. It was so flavorful, but somehow subtle at the same time. This recipe is now on a sticky note on the front of my recipe binder. I will be making it a lot.

I had a big round steak that I wanted to do ~something~ with but couldn't decide what. I doubled this recipe and put it in this marinade overnight. When it was time to eat I cut the steak in half and seared one half of it on both sides in a ribbed skillet. I didn't want it to be well done. It was FANTASTIC!!! I served it with a bed of romain lettuce. The dressing I created for that was just a plop of real mayo, a small orange cut up, some slivered onions and sugar. I let that dressing weep together for about an 30 minutes while I fixed the lettuce and the meat. Thats it. It was also FANTASTIC and went beautifully next to this Ginger steak! Tonight: Repeat of last night to use up (oh darn) the other half of that steak! I can only imagine how delicious it will be after being in the marinade for another 24 hours!!!

This is a phenom recipe. I've been making it for about 3 years and it is a huge family favorite. The only changes I make are to increase the ginger and garlic (there's never enough), as well as the maple syrup (up to 1/2 cup). I also boil the marinade for a great sauce (wonderful on mashed potatoes). Thank you SO much William for sharing this amazing recipe!
I used flank instead of rib eye ,Left one in over night was good but left one in for 3 days better much more tender and full of flavor

Delicious and easy! It was my first time making steak, so I was a little nervous, but it turned out great. I marinated for 3 hours, and followed others' suggestions and reduced the remaining marinade and used it as a sauce. I didn't have mustard seed so I left it out, but my marinade and sauce turned out wonderfully. Highly recommended!

Awesome recipe! I used a little less soy sauce because I wanted to reduce the salt some. The steak was nice and tender and really soaked up the flavour (I marinated overnight). I also boiled the marinade and mixed that with sauteed mushrooms and onions and served that over the steak. Turned out fantastic. I'll make again for sure.
This marinade is mouth watering delicious! I omit the beer and let it marinate for 2 days!

This marinade is absolutely delicious.The only thing I would suggest is:NEVER cut into a steak to see if it is done.Let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes for the juices to redistribute.The temperature will rise and it will finish cooking.Otherwise you'll get a plate of blood.
I have used this marinade on Rib eyes and flank with excellent flavors. I suggest using a wheat (weiss beer) beer or Ale which pairs well with the steak.
Excellent marinade, very tasty. Everyone in the family liked it. I let it marinade overnight overnight in the fridge and will do that again
This was a good marinade for the steaks, they came out flavorful and tender, will use again...FYI steaks didn’t need any salt or pepper, it was that good.
Just a little sweet for me but overall I loved it. Next time I'll add a little extra hot sauce and some garlic salt
This was good. It had a kind of asian flare. I think if I make it again, I'll up the maple syrup. I think it needs a little more sweetness.
Not good. Disappointing marinade.

First time making steak in about 30 years. Made this recipe for dinner and even after being stuffed people were going back for more. I also cooked the marinade down and added a bit of cornstarch for a dressing over rice. Will definitely be making this again.
